blocks.text: [F] Sandur Manganese & Iron Ores (SMIORE) is a 1954-incorporated merchant miner of low-phosphorus manganese ore and 56-58% Fe iron ore from two captive leases (1,999 ha) in Sandur, Ballari district, Karnataka, both valid until 31 December 2033 (AR2026 p.17, p.21-22). [F] It converts part of its manganese ore into silicomanganese/ferromanganese (95,000 TPA SiMn capacity), runs a 0.5 MTPA non-recovery coke oven with 32 MW of waste-heat power at Vyasanakere, and since 11 November 2024 consolidates Arjas Steel (98.94%), a 0.585 MTPA Special Bar Quality (SBQ) and alloy steel maker with plants at Tadipatri (Andhra Pradesh) and Mandi Gobindgarh (Punjab) (AR2026 p.14, p.24, p.303). [F] FY26 consolidated revenue was Rs 5,088 cr, EBITDA Rs 1,208 cr (24%) and PAT Rs 658 cr (NUMBERS).

[F] How it makes money: ores are sold to end users (steel makers and ferroalloy producers) and revenue on ore is recognised on completion of e-auction and receipt of money (AR2026 p.186); [MC] management described the entire ore sales as being through e-auction under the Monitoring Committee regime and Karnataka iron ore export as effectively barred (CALL Jul 2021). [F] Steel is sold B2B to automotive OEMs and their supply chains, none named (AR2026 p.9, p.25). [F] Coke has moved from merchant sales to a conversion contract with one unnamed 'marquee customer' covering ~46% of capacity (AR2026 p.23, p.40).

[F] Customer profile: B2B steel manufacturers and ferroalloy producers (AR2026 p.127); one customer exceeded 10% of consolidated revenue in both FY26 and FY25 but is neither named nor quantified (AR2026 p.299). [AI] Effectively 100% of revenue is a derivative of Indian steel demand, so 'diversification' into steel diversifies the product, not the end market.

Listing status and evidence base: [F] the company has been listed on BSE since 1966 and is now also on NSE (AR2026 p.17-18); this is not a recent listing. [F] The evidence base is thin on management dialogue: the only earnings-call transcripts available to us are from July 2019 (a one-on-one analyst meeting) and July 2021; no FY26 or Q1 FY27 call transcript was available. Current-quarter management commentary comes from the August 2026 investor presentation (PPT Aug 2026). No prospectus or offer document was available.

blocks.text: [AI] Driver classification: #1 and #2 are company-specific (lease-specific and approval-specific) but time-bound by the 2033 lease expiry; #3 and #6 are company-specific; #4 and #5 are cyclical (steel spreads, ferroalloy prices, coal prices); #7 is cyclical (trailing multiples on cycle-dependent earnings). None is genuinely structural beyond 2033, because the profit pool rests on a lease that will be re-awarded by auction (RATING).

items: 1. **The mining profit pool has a hard expiry.** [F] Both leases expire 31 December 2033 and renewal will be via competitive auction (AR2026 p.17; RATING). [F] Mining PBT of Rs 862.7 cr exceeded group PBT (AR2026 p.297). [AI] Any perpetuity-style valuation implicitly assumes the company re-wins its own leases at similar economics, which nothing in the documents supports.

2. **A near-dated forest-clearance problem.** [F] On 30 Apr 2026 the Karnataka High Court dismissed SMIORE's writ against a Deputy Conservator of Forests demand for compensatory afforestation charges plus land as a condition of extending forest leases beyond December 2026; an SLP to the Supreme Court is planned; no provision, and not in contingent liabilities (AR2026 p.313). [F] The amount is Rs 131.25 cr in the notes and RATING but Rs 13,905 lakh (Rs 139.05 cr) in the Board's report (AR2026 p.74, p.313) - not reconciled.

3. **Capital is migrating from a high-return mine to a low-return steel business.** [F] Steel segment assets Rs 3,668 cr earned segment PBT Rs 202 cr in FY26; mining assets Rs 342 cr earned Rs 863 cr (AR2026 p.297-299). [E] Steel holds ~66% of segment assets and earns ~5.5% pre-tax on them.

4. **Ore realisations are falling.** [F] FY26 iron ore realisation Rs 3,128/t vs Rs 3,510/t; manganese ore Rs 6,486/t vs Rs 8,090/t (AR2026 p.40); iron ore revenue fell to Rs 1,230.7 cr from Rs 1,392.5 cr despite +2% volumes (AR2026 p.284).

5. **Organic growth has stalled; headline growth is acquisition arithmetic.** [F] TTM sales are only 4.7% above FY26 (NUMBERS); [F] standalone revenue rose 3.7% to Rs 2,010.6 cr (AR2026 p.62). [E] Roughly Rs 1,674 cr of the Rs 1,922 cr steel revenue increase in FY26 is the annualisation of Arjas (FY25 full-year Arjas revenue Rs 2,884 cr per AR2026 p.40 vs Rs 1,210 cr consolidated).

6. **Regulatory tax overhang.** [F] CRISIL flags the Karnataka (Minerals Rights and Mineral Bearing Land) Tax Bill, 2024, with royalty-linked payments retrospective from 2005 payable over 12 years, pending Presidential assent; a 'significantly higher-than-expected' tax is a rating downgrade trigger (RATING). [F] The annual report does not mention this bill at all (AR2026, whole document searched). [F] Forest Development Tax contingent liability Rs 100.8 cr (AR2026 p.289).

7. **Managerial pay is rising far faster than the business.** [F] MD remuneration ~Rs 22.6 cr in FY26, +161.67% YoY, 379x median employee; median employee pay +2.38% and non-managerial average pay -1.42% (AR2026 p.96, p.106). [F] Standalone PAT grew 22% (AR2026 p.62).

8. **Thin disclosure on what matters.** [F] No named customers, no order book, no segment EBITDA, the >10% customer unnamed, coke conversion counterparty unnamed (AR2026 p.23, p.299). [F] No earnings call transcript since 2021 was available to us.

9. **The DCF base case already embeds aggressive growth.** [F] Base DCF Rs 171.3 assumes 30% starting growth fading to 10% at a 25% margin; the price of Rs 178 needs 22.1% five-year sales CAGR (NUMBERS). [AI] Disclosed capacity cannot deliver that without new projects or acquisitions.

**Is this a miner or a steel company?** [F] Revenue says steel (61.5% of FY26 product revenue) but profit says mining (segment PBT Rs 863 cr vs steel Rs 202 cr) (AR2026 p.284, p.297). [AI] The market may be applying a cyclical steel multiple to what is mostly a time-limited mining annuity - which cuts both ways: too high if 2033 is ignored, too low if mining cash is valued for its near-term certainty.

**Is 2033 a cliff or an option?** [F] Leases expire 31 Dec 2033 and re-award is by auction (RATING). [AI] An incumbent with geological data, infrastructure (downhill conveyor, railway sidings) and a 7-Star rated mine is well placed to bid, but auction premiums typically transfer much of the rent to the state; the documents give no basis to estimate post-2033 economics.

**Is Arjas a value trap or a re-rating lever?** [F] Arjas EBITDA rose 85% to Rs 351 cr and EBITDA/t rose to ~Rs 8,645 (AR2026 p.40). [AI] The market may underappreciate that SBQ is a niche with OEM empanelment barriers; equally it may underappreciate that 11% EBITDA margins on Rs 3,668 cr of assets plus Rs 340 cr goodwill do not cover a 14.3% WACC.

**Is the low ore realisation the bottom?** [MC] Management says prices bottomed in Q2-Q3 FY26 and April 2026 benchmarks support a better FY27 (AR2026 p.62); [F] Q1 FY27 manganese realisation rose 15% QoQ to Rs 7,954/t and iron ore 9% to Rs 3,095/t (PPT Aug 2026). [AI] One quarter is not a trend; iron ore remains below the FY26 average of Rs 3,128/t.

**Is the forest-clearance demand a nuisance or existential?** [F] Rs 131.25 cr is ~20% of FY26 PAT (AR2026 p.313; NUMBERS) [E]. [AI] Paying it is affordable; the real risk is operational interruption if forest clearance beyond December 2026 lapses while the SLP is pending - the documents do not say what happens to operations in that event.

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus framing (and our own earlier board note) is a 'mineral-lease moat' with downstream integration lifting returns (BOARD). The documents support the first half and contradict the second: downstream integration has so far diluted returns - ferroalloys made Rs 10 cr PBT, coke & energy Rs 10 cr and steel Rs 202 cr on combined segment assets of ~Rs 4,330 cr, against Rs 863 cr from a Rs 342 cr mine (AR2026 p.297-299) [E]. Our variant view is that SMIORE is best understood as a seven-year mining cash annuity (to Dec 2033) being recycled into a steel business whose standalone returns are below the cost of capital, and that the trailing 12x P/E (NUMBERS) is not cheap once the lease horizon is respected - but neither is the stock obviously expensive, because the base DCF (Rs 171.3) is within 4% of the price (NUMBERS). The swing factor is not the next quarter's ore price but whether the steel arm can earn its capital before the mine's cash flows end.

blocks.text: [F] Sources: AOC-1 and Board's report (AR2026 p.62, p.78-79), group composition note (AR2026 p.312-313), related-party note (AR2026 p.299), ANNOUNCEMENTS. Standalone PAT Rs 543.08 cr per Board's report table (AR2026 p.62). [F] Arjas Steel and Arjas Modern Steel carry negative reserves of Rs (913.5) cr and Rs (151.4) cr respectively (AR2026 p.78). [F] Royal Sandur Hospitality and Royal Sandur Academy are described as being incorporated (PPT Aug 2026); no incorporation filing for either is in the announcements we hold.

[AI] The mine is 120 years old, but the business investors are buying is less than three years old. The iron ore volume step-up (1.6 to 4.45 MTPA) dates from FY24-FY26, the steel business from November 2024, and the coke conversion model from April 2025 (AR2026 p.23, p.64; PPT Aug 2026). [F] Of the ten years in our statements data, FY20 and FY21 are missing and the FY22 balance sheet is blank (NUMBERS), so the long history cannot be fully tested. [AI] The company has a history of large ambitions delivered late: a 1 MTPA steel plant was talked about in 2008, 2017 and 2021 (CALL Jul 2019; CALL Jul 2021) and steel was ultimately bought, not built. The new 'Royal Sandur' umbrella with hospitality, academy and medtech ventures (PPT Aug 2026; ANNOUNCEMENTS) suggests the diversification agenda ahead of the 2033 lease expiry is broadening rather than focusing.

items: 1. Mining: [F] iron ore from fully mechanised operations, manganese ore from semi-mechanised, labour-intensive pocket deposits (PPT Aug 2026; CALL Jul 2019); earth-moving uses contractors on a tonnage basis, which management calls an 'asset-light model' (CALL Jul 2021).

2. Evacuation: [F] ore moved to railway sidings at Swamihalli and Sunderambencha (AR2026 p.19); [MC] the 1.2 km downhill pipe conveyor to the railway siding is completed and capitalised, with commercial operations targeted by Q2 FY27 (PPT Aug 2026).

3. Sale or captive use: [F] ores sold via e-auction to end users (AR2026 p.186); 0.61 LT of manganese ore used captively in FY26 (AR2026 p.21); iron ore now also supplied to Arjas Tadipatri (AR2026 p.10, p.25).
4. Ferroalloys: [F] manganese ore plus power converted into SiMn/FeMn in submerged arc furnaces; 2 of 3 furnaces running (AR2026 p.9, p.41).

5. Coke & energy: [F] non-recovery coke ovens produce coke and waste heat for 32 MW WHRB power that feeds the ferroalloy furnaces; FY26 output was almost entirely conversion for a customer (2,22,575 t conversion vs 869 t own) (AR2026 p.40); [MC] no by-products other than power (CALL Jul 2021).

blocks.text: [F] Value is captured overwhelmingly at the mine: mining segment PBT margin was 52% of segment revenue in FY26 versus 2.7% for ferroalloys, 7.3% for coke & energy and 6.4% for steel (AR2026 p.297-299) [E]. [AI] The reason is economic rent: the ore body is a state-granted lease with low extraction cost, and royalty and other taxes (Rs 481.6 cr in FY26, AR2026 p.287) are the main way the state shares it. Downstream stages are conversion businesses that buy power, coal and scrap at market prices and sell into competitive markets. [MC] Management's thesis is that integration ('mines to metals') captures conversion margin (AR2026 p.3, p.19); [AI] on FY26 segment disclosure, the conversion margin is thin and the benefit of captive ore to Arjas is not quantified.

[MC] Mining is described as 'asset-light' because earth-moving is contracted (CALL Jul 2021; PPT Aug 2026). [F] Mining segment assets were Rs 341.9 cr vs steel Rs 3,668.0 cr (AR2026 p.297). [F] Consolidated fixed-asset turnover fell from 2.42x in FY23 to 1.01x in FY25 and 1.54x in FY26 (NUMBERS). [AI] The group has shifted from asset-light to capital-heavy: the acquisition added Rs 1,884.5 cr of PPE and Rs 200.5 cr of CWIP at fair value (AR2026 p.303). The capital intensity now sits in the lower-return segment.

subsections.title: Export mix, currency and trade policy

items: [AI] The fall in exports from 3.0% to 1.1% of revenue looks like mix (bigger domestic denominator plus lower export volume), not strategy; no export strategy is articulated.

[F] Currency exposure is small and 'predominantly in US dollars'; no hedging; total commodity exposure stated as Nil because coking coal was not imported under the conversion model (AR2026 p.116). [F] FX loss of Rs 2.84 cr in FY26 (AR2026 p.285).

[AI] Indirect currency exposure is larger than direct: domestic iron ore and manganese prices follow import parity and international benchmarks (AR2026 p.37 cites Platts IODEX and China manganese spot prices).

[F] Trade policy: iron ore export from Karnataka is restricted (CALL Jul 2021); a quantitative restriction on low-ash met coke ran to 31 Dec 2025 and was replaced in January 2026 by a provisional anti-dumping duty of $60.87-130.6/t (AR2026 p.39); MD&A flags EU CBAM and West Asia conflict as geopolitical risks (AR2026 p.42). [AI] The coke anti-dumping duty is a tailwind for restarting the idle batteries.

summary.one_line: Sandur is a high-return, lease-bound Karnataka mining cash stream being recycled into a lower-return steel business; at Rs 178 the price sits just above our base-case DCF value of Rs 171.3, which already assumes growth that disclosed capacity cannot deliver and ignores the December 2033 lease expiry and near-dated forest-clearance and state-tax risks.

[F] Deleveraging is largely done: borrowings fell to Rs 994.8 cr from Rs 1,882.2 cr after early redemption of Rs 423 cr NCDs, and CRISIL revised its A+ outlook to Positive on 2 Jun 2026 (AR2026 p.277; RATING).
[F] Cash conversion is strong: CFO/PAT 1.74x in FY26 and 1.56x over three years; FY26 FCF Rs 988 cr (NUMBERS).
[F] Arjas steel EBITDA rose 85% to Rs 351 cr and EBITDA/t to ~Rs 8,645 in FY26; Q1 FY27 steel realisation was up 6% QoQ (AR2026 p.40; PPT Aug 2026).
[F] Ore prices may have turned: Q1 FY27 manganese realisation +15% QoQ and iron ore +9% QoQ, with Q1 PAT +36.5% YoY (PPT Aug 2026; NUMBERS).
bear_points: [F] Both mining leases expire 31 Dec 2033 and will be re-awarded by auction (AR2026 p.17; RATING); [AI] the DCF treats the mining cash flows as perpetual.

[F] The Karnataka High Court dismissed the company's challenge to a compensatory afforestation demand that conditions forest-clearance extension beyond December 2026; the demand is unprovided and quoted at Rs 131.25 cr in the notes and Rs 139.05 cr in the Board's report (AR2026 p.74, p.313).

[F] The reverse DCF requires 22.1% five-year sales CAGR vs a 19.8% base case (NUMBERS); [E] full utilisation of disclosed capacity at Q1 FY27 prices supports ~Rs 7,100 cr of revenue, ~6% CAGR.

[F] Governance signals are weak: MD pay rose 161.67% to ~Rs 22.6 cr (379x median), FY25 political donation of Rs 9.75 cr, and a retrospective Karnataka mineral tax bill flagged by CRISIL is not mentioned in the annual report (AR2026 p.96, p.106, p.213; RATING).
